summary:
**Combustion Safety Console** is an AI-powered interactive dashboard designed to transform NASA’s complex combustion research into accessible, data-driven fire safety insights for human space exploration.

Our platform uses Python, Flask, and OpenAI-powered Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to process experimental datasets, scientific reports, and metadata. Users can explore investigations, visualize experimental results through interactive graphs, compare findings, and ask an AI assistant questions that are answered using scientific evidence and source citations. The system also provides transparent relevance rankings and highlights important research findings and limitations.

This project addresses NASA’s *Flame in Freefall* challenge by making microgravity combustion research easier to search, understand, compare, and interpret. It helps researchers and engineers identify potential fire hazards and explore prevention, detection, and suppression strategies for spacecraft, space stations, and future Moon and Mars habitats.

Our prototype demonstrates these capabilities using three representative NASA investigations, with a scalable architecture designed to incorporate additional research. Ultimately, our goal is to make scientific knowledge more accessible and support safer human space exploration.
details:
Project Details — Combustion Safety Console

Combustion Safety Console is an interactive, AI-powered web platform developed to make NASA’s microgravity combustion research more accessible, understandable, and useful for improving fire safety in human space exploration.

How Our Project Works

NASA has conducted decades of combustion experiments, producing extensive scientific reports, experimental datasets, and technical documentation. However, extracting meaningful insights from these resources can be time-consuming, especially when information is distributed across different formats and investigations.

Our platform addresses this challenge by transforming complex research materials into an organized, searchable, and interactive dashboard.

The system processes NASA research documents, including PDFs, CSV datasets, metadata, and DOCX files, using a Python-based preprocessing pipeline. This information is structured and connected to an AI assistant powered by OpenAI's API through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

Rather than relying solely on the AI model's general knowledge, our system retrieves relevant information directly from the processed research materials. This allows users to ask scientific questions and receive context-aware responses supported by source references.

Users can:

  • Explore investigations: Browse NASA combustion experiments, examine their objectives, experimental conditions, measurements, and findings.
  • Visualize experimental data: Generate interactive charts from actual measurements, with selectable variables and hoverable data points.
  • Interact with an AI research assistant: Ask questions about individual investigations or across multiple experiments and receive evidence-based explanations.
  • Compare investigations: Identify similarities and differences in experimental conditions, materials, measurements, and results.
  • Rank research relevance: Discover which investigations are most relevant to specific fire safety questions through a transparent ranking system.
  • Explore fire safety implications: Understand how experimental findings may inform prevention, detection, and suppression strategies in space environments.

Technologies and Tools Used

Our project was developed using a lightweight, modular software architecture:

  • Python: Processes research files, extracts information, prepares experimental datasets, and manages scientific evidence.
  • Flask: Provides the backend REST API connecting the research data, AI services, and website.
  • OpenAI API: Powers the AI research assistant and supports evidence-based interpretation through RAG.
  • SQLite: Stores semantic search embeddings locally to support efficient information retrieval.
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Build the interactive, responsive web interface.
  • Chart.js: Displays interactive scientific graphs and visualizations.
  • Git: Supports source-code version control and collaborative development.

The platform is entirely software-based and does not require specialized hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

Our project's innovation lies in combining scientific data visualization, AI-assisted research, and explainable evidence ranking within one accessible platform.

Instead of presenting users with static reports or generic AI-generated explanations, Combustion Safety Console connects scientific measurements with their original research context.

A particularly important feature is its approach to AI-generated visualizations. The assistant can select appropriate experimental variables and request charts, while the backend constructs the graphs using actual recorded measurements. This prevents the AI from inventing numerical data.

Additionally, our platform accounts for differences in dataset structures, measurement units, missing information, and experimental conditions, allowing research from different sources to be explored through a consistent interface.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Fire behaves differently in microgravity, making fire safety a critical concern for spacecraft, space stations, lunar and Martian habitats, and other crewed environments.

By simplifying access to NASA's experimental findings, our platform aims to reduce the effort required to investigate combustion behavior, compare research results, and identify evidence relevant to future fire safety technologies.

The system is intended to support researchers, engineers, students, and mission planners in understanding fire hazards and exploring potential improvements to fire detection, prevention, and suppression.

It also makes complex scientific research more approachable for educational purposes, helping users engage with real NASA experimental data without requiring extensive experience in data processing.

Development Considerations and Future Potential

Throughout development, our team prioritized scientific accuracy, transparency, usability, performance, security, and scalability.

We designed the AI to distinguish between measured experimental results, interpretations, and research limitations. Source citations help users trace answers back to the original evidence, while transparent rankings avoid presenting relevance scores as definitive safety assessments.

We also considered performance through preprocessing, caching, and efficient retrieval, as well as security by keeping API credentials on the backend.

Our current prototype demonstrates the complete research pipeline using three representative NASA investigations. Its modular architecture allows additional experiments and research documents to be incorporated in the future.

While the platform provides evidence-based qualitative insights, it does not claim to produce validated numerical fire predictions or replace established engineering safety assessments.

Our long-term vision is to transform NASA's extensive combustion research into a scalable, intelligent scientific resource that supports better-informed fire safety decisions and contributes to safer human exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
